target_question: Find mathematical law families that resemble: polynomially find the next correct small state/key, preserve exact semantics, and guarantee polynomial progress to termination.
scientific_boundary: No cited result proves a universal polynomial-time route law for arbitrary CNF SAT.
Restricted-class tractability does not imply SAT in P.
FPT in a structural parameter does not become polynomial unless that parameter is globally bounded by O(log n) or a constant in the needed exponent regime.
Monotone local progress alone does not imply polynomial trajectory length.
Existence of a short proof/representation does not imply polynomial-time discovery.

source.title: Satisfiability of Acyclic and Almost Acyclic CNF Formulas
source.authors: Sebastian Ordyniak, Daniel Paulusma, Stefan Szeider

law_families.law: For beta-acyclic CNF, Davis-Putnam elimination can follow variables whose resolvents remain subsets of parent clauses; elimination does not increase formula size and removes a variable each step.

janus_mapping.POLY_FIND: On beta-acyclic instances the appropriate structural elimination behavior is recognizable/constructible in polynomial time.
janus_mapping.POLY_HOLD: For a weakly/DP-simplicial elimination step, DP_x(F) does not exceed the parent formula size in the tractable setting.
janus_mapping.POLY_ADVANCE: One variable is eliminated per step, hence at most n eliminations.

law_families.killer_barrier: The broader class of formulas admitting some DP-simplicial elimination ordering has NP-complete membership: several locally legal-looking variables may exist and choosing the globally right continuation can itself encode SAT.

sources.title: Weaker consistency notions for all the CSPs of bounded width
Local consistency as a reduction between constraint satisfaction problems

law_families.law: For bounded-width CSP languages, a fixed level/type of local consistency is sufficient to decide global satisfiability in polynomial time.

janus_mapping.progress: domain/constraint pruning until contradiction or globally extendible state
janus_mapping.theorem_shape: LOCAL_CERTIFIED_CONSISTENCY => GLOBAL_SOLVABILITY for a characterized language class

law_families.killer_barrier: Arbitrary SAT/CSP is not bounded-width; the algebraic structural property is the substantive restriction.

sources.title: A Fixed-Parameter Algorithm for #SAT with Parameter Incidence Treewidth
An Improved Parameterized Algorithm for Treewidth
Compilation and Fast Model Counting beyond CNF
Courcelle's Theorem in Truly Linear FPT

law_families.law: If a suitable decomposition has bounded width k, dynamic programming/compilation maintains states exponential only in k and polynomial in input size; fixed k gives polynomial/linear-FPT behavior.

janus_mapping.POLY_FIND: Tree decompositions of width k can be found by FPT algorithms such as 2^{O(k^2)} n^{O(1)}; for fixed k this is polynomial.
janus_mapping.POLY_HOLD: bag/interface state is bounded by f(k) poly(n)

law_families.killer_barrier: For unrestricted CNF, k may grow with n, converting f(k) into exponential cost. A universal proof would need a width-like parameter provably small for every CNF or a different route when it is large.

law_families.law: Find a small set/depth of decisions that sends every or some relevant residual instance into a polynomial-time tractable base class, then solve there.

janus_mapping.route: bounded branching depth into Horn/Krom/acyclic tractable region

law_families.killer_barrier: Backdoor detection is hard in general for important target classes (including W[2]-hard cases); bounded distance is a structural promise, not a universal theorem for all CNFs.

source.title: The Power of Self-Reducibility: Selectivity, Information, and Approximation

law_families.law: SAT search can fix variables one by one with polynomially many queries to a SAT decision procedure; the residual instance shrinks monotonically.

janus_mapping.POLY_HOLD: partial assignment plus residual formula remains polynomial-size
janus_mapping.POLY_ADVANCE: one variable fixed per stage, O(n) stages
janus_mapping.missing_piece: POLY_FIND of the correct branch requires the SAT decision capability itself

law_families.killer_barrier: This is not a SAT algorithm without a decision oracle; it relocates the hard bit into each branch query.

sources.title: Information in propositional proofs and algorithmic proof search

law_families.law: Short certificates can exist while finding a comparably short Resolution refutation is computationally hard; proof existence and proof discovery are distinct resources.

janus_mapping.target: Any JANUS route law relying on 'there is a short proof nearby' must include a polynomial proof-search theorem.

law_families.killer_barrier: Resolution is not automatizable unless P=NP; finding a refutation polynomially related to the shortest one is NP-hard.

source.title: PLS-complete problems with lexicographic cost functions: Max-k-SAT and Abelian Permutation Orbit Minimization

law_families.law: A neighborhood may be polynomially searchable and every accepted move may strictly improve a potential, yet reaching a local optimum need not have a polynomial step bound.

janus_mapping.POLY_FIND: next improving neighbor can be locally specified/searchable
janus_mapping.failure: POLY_ADVANCE can still fail because the potential range/path height is exponential

law_families.killer_barrier: A strictly monotone measure is insufficient; JANUS needs a polynomially bounded rank or a guaranteed polynomial decrease in a bounded numeric quantity, with bit complexity charged.

sources.title: Exponential Lower Bounds for Many Pivot Rules for the Simplex Method
An Exponential Lower Bound for Zadeh's pivot rule

law_families.law: Compact states plus locally valid improving pivots do not ensure a strongly polynomial global trajectory; many natural pivot rules have exponential worst cases.
law_families.janus_mapping: The 'choose next exact local transformation' problem is structurally analogous to choosing a pivot rule: local correctness is easy, universal path-length control is the hard theorem.
law_families.killer_barrier: For simplex, existence of a pivot rule guaranteeing strongly polynomial runtime remains a longstanding open problem, despite LP itself being polynomial-time solvable by other methods.

source.title: Succinct progress measures for solving parity games

law_families.law: Encode a well-founded progress order compactly and repeatedly lift states until a fixed point; the size/range of the progress domain controls termination complexity.

janus_mapping.candidate: Attach rank mu(K) drawn from a certified finite ordered domain and require every nonterminal transition to decrease/increase monotonically toward a bound.
janus_mapping.lesson: Compression of the rank domain can improve complexity, but the cited parity-game result is quasi-polynomial, not the polynomial SAT theorem we need.

law_families.killer_barrier: A progress measure is useful only if its representation, update, and total number of distinct admissible rank values are all polynomially bounded.

sources.title: Sparsification Upper and Lower Bounds for Graph Problems and Not-All-Equal SAT
Strong Sparsification for 1-in-3-SAT via Polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa
On Kernelization with Access to NP-Oracles

law_families.law: Polynomial preprocessing can sometimes reduce redundant structure while preserving the decision problem, but strong compression has conditional lower bounds and problem-specific limits.
law_families.janus_mapping: A Magic Key compression step must prove that the reduced state is equivalent, small, polynomially discoverable, and not hiding an NP oracle or nonuniform advice.
law_families.killer_barrier: There is no general license to assume every NP-hard instance has a substantially smaller polynomial-time discoverable equivalent encoding under standard complexity assumptions.

topa_spider_synthesis.strongest_positive_template: BETA_ACYCLIC_DP_SIMPLICIAL_ELIMINATION: locally recognizable elimination, non-growing representation, one-variable progress. This is almost exactly the JANUS desired law, but only on a tractable structural class.
topa_spider_synthesis.strongest_local_to_global_template: BOUNDED_WIDTH_CSP: a fixed local-consistency rule is guaranteed to settle globally all instances from a characterized tractable language family.
topa_spider_synthesis.strongest_discovery_barrier: RESOLUTION_AUTOMATIZATION: a short target proof can exist while finding a near-shortest proof is NP-hard.
topa_spider_synthesis.strongest_trajectory_barrier: PLS/SIMPLEX: compact states plus polynomial local moves plus strict improvement can still generate exponentially long trajectories.
topa_spider_synthesis.strongest_width_barrier: TREEWIDTH/BACKDOORS: strong route laws exist when a structural parameter is bounded, but the parameter or its discovery cost can become the exponential resource on unrestricted inputs.
topa_spider_synthesis.main_gap: No arXiv result found supplies a single uniform polynomially computable next-move law with polynomial state size and polynomially bounded progress rank for every CNF formula.
topa_spider_synthesis.candidate_meta_lemma: If there exist polynomial-time computable NEXT(F,K), exact transition semantics, a polynomial p with |K|<=p(|F|), and an integer rank mu(F,K) in [0,p(|F|)] that strictly decreases on every nonterminal transition, then the resulting trajectory has polynomial length and polynomial total transition cost provided each transition is polynomial. The lemma is elementary; finding such NEXT and mu for arbitrary SAT is the unresolved substance.

recommended_r5_attack_order.question: Can JANUS define a polynomially recognizable local elimination predicate strictly broader than known beta-acyclic/DP-simplicial-safe classes while preserving a non-growth invariant?
recommended_r5_attack_order.failure_signal: Recognizing whether a safe elimination continuation exists becomes NP-hard or selected eliminations cause superpolynomial state growth.

recommended_r5_attack_order.question: Can every nonterminal CNF state be assigned a polynomial-bit rank mu<=poly(n), computable in polytime, such that the selected exact next step strictly decreases it?
recommended_r5_attack_order.failure_signal: Rank requires exponential numeric range/precision, is not poly-computable, or admits exponentially many unit decreases.

recommended_r5_attack_order.question: For each candidate representation/proof/backdoor/decomposition, distinguish EXISTS_SMALL from FIND_SMALL and charge the latter independently.
recommended_r5_attack_order.failure_signal: Route selection reduces to known hard discovery/automatization problems.

recommended_r5_attack_order.question: When treewidth/backdoor depth/representation width grows, require a certified switch to another route whose own parameter is small, without circular discovery or cumulative switching blowup.
recommended_r5_attack_order.failure_signal: There exists a family where all portfolio parameters become large or finding which parameter is small is itself hard.
